newsitem.title: UK: Insurers need local partner for Vietnam - industry.
newsitem.headline: Insurers need local partner for Vietnam - industry.

text.p: Vietnam is ready to open up to outside investment, but insurers looking to enter the market will need to do so through joint ventures, Commercial Union Plc Director Michael Ridding said on Monday.

"The country is ready to change and open its market to foreign insurers, but foreign direct participation may be limited to joint ventures for the foreseeable future," he told a meeting of the Insurance Institute of London.
Commercial Union last month announced the first insurance joint venture in Vietnam, between itself, local insurer Bao Viet and Tokio Fire and Marine Insurance Company.
The company, Vietnam International Assurance Company, will initially concentrate on insuring foreign joint venture business.
Most opportunities are seen in the construction and engineering sectors as the country works to improve its infrastructure.
The local insurance market is small at around $100 million a year, but Vietnam has one of the fastest growing economies in Asia. "Vietnam has a burning desire to improve its lot," Ridding said.
Bao Viet was the sole insurer between 1975 and 1994 and still dominates the market with an 80 percent market share.
However, other Vietnamese insurers have been established and some 24 foreign insurers and five brokers now have representative offices in the country.
Energy and marine insurance account for around 30 percent of premiums, with only a very limited market for personal and life insurance due to the very low per capita income of around $200 a year.
"The market is changing, but it is only at the first stage of development. Regulation and codes of conduct are needed," Ridding said.
An insurance law is expected in the next few years, possibly in 1999, and the European Union is helping with the drafting of legislation for the industry as well as with training.
